linguistics.meaning: Six Shooter — the ‘little six-er’, a six-cartridge revolver

morphemes.gloss: numeral root: ‘six’ — the same root in nikotwâsik / nikocwâsik ‘six (count)’ and in nikotwâs‑mitanaw ‘sixty.’ The cw cluster here reflects the Plains-Cree palatalised dialectal variant of tw.
noun medial: ‘bone, hard projecting thing’ (as in oskan ‘bone’) — used here for the cylindrical chamber-and-barrel of the revolver, the ‘hard six-piece’ of the gun.
diminutive final: ‘small, little’ — the productive ‑ôs / ‑sis ending that marks something small or familiar (cf. kâkwasis ‘little porcupine’, atimosis ‘puppy’).

relatedForms.english: Six (the bare numeral, ‘there are six of them’)

morphemes.gloss: initial: ‘one, single’ — the underlying ‘one’ root that combines with ‑wâsik to form ‘six’
VII final: ‘there are X of them’ used in numeral words

relatedForms.note: The free-standing word for ‘six’. In Plains Cree the tw cluster is widely realised as cw (palatalised), so nikotwâsik and nikocwâsik are both heard.

morphemes.gloss: verb stem: ‘to shoot, to make a sharp/burst sound’

relatedForms.note: Literally ‘the shooting-thing.’ This is the generic word for gun; nikocwâsaskanôs is the specifically-six-shot diminutive for a revolver.

relatedForms.english: Bone (the bare noun, source of the ‑askan‑ medial)

morphemes.gloss: NI noun: ‘bone, hard projecting/protruding thing’ — surfaces inside the headword as the medial ‑askan‑, naming the cylinder/barrel as the gun’s ‘hard six-piece’.

relatedForms.note: The metaphor is body-part: a revolver is named for its hard, six-chambered bone-like cylinder.

culturalStory.heading: About nikocwâsaskanôs — the Little Six-Shot
body: On the wall the nikocwâsaskanôs plaque sits directly under the mistâpiskihkomân (Machete) plaque, sharing the same white-and-black palette: a long single-action revolver in black silhouette with a bone-handle grip, the syllabics ᓂᑯᒑᐧᓴᐢᑲᓅᐢ carved in red across the chamber, and ‘SIX SHOOTER’ in big letters underneath.

The Cree word reads three pieces deep. nikocwâs‑ is the numeral ‘six’ (the standard nikotwâsik, with the local Plains Cree palatalisation tw → cw that you hear across Edmonton). ‑askan‑ is the body-part medial ‘bone, hard projecting thing,’ the same medial in oskan ‘bone’; here it names the cylinder-and-barrel as the gun’s hard six-piece. The diminutive ‑ôs at the end means ‘small, little.’ Read together: ‘the little six-shot.’

The trail of the same name flows along the south side of the river toward Emily Murphy Park in NW Edmonton. Trailforks rates it blue with a 1.1 km roll-and-pump style, named — like its neighbours Rich Kid, Plan B, and Machete — in the cowboy/outlaw register that the local builders favour for this stretch. The land is ᓀᐦᐃᔭᐤ ᐊᐢᑭᕀ Nêhiyaw‑Askiy (Plains Cree territory), and Trailforks itself lists the AKA ᓂᑯᒑᐧᓴᐢᑲᓅᐢ nikocwâsaskanôs for this trail — the same form carved on the plaque.

notes: PHYSICAL SIGN OVERRIDES CATALOGUE (syllabics): The plaque carving and Trailforks both write the syllabics as 'ᓂᑯᒑᐧᓴᐢᑲᓅᐢ' (with ᒑᐧ for cwâ and ᓅ for nô). The current catalogue creeSyllabics 'ᓂᑯᐚᓴᐢᑲᓄᐢ' is missing the c-glyph and the long-ô on the diminutive. Coordinator should update catalogue creeSyllabics to ᓂᑯᒑᐧᓴᐢᑲᓅᐢ. The catalogue creeName 'nikocwâsaskanôs' is already correct.

Morpheme bracketing nikocwâs‑askan‑ôs is the structural reading: numeral six + bone-medial + diminutive. An alternative reading parses the word as nikocwâs‑askanôs where ‑askanôs is a frozen ‘small bone-thing’ noun; both readings yield the same surface form, but the three-morpheme split is preferred here because the ‑askan‑ medial is independently productive in Cree word-formation (as in oskan).
The cw cluster in nikocwâsaskanôs reflects the local Plains Cree palatalisation of tw → cw (so nikotwâsik ‘six’ → nikocwâsik). Both forms are widely heard across nehiyaw-askiy.
The diminutive ‑ôs is a regular Plains Cree diminutive ending; for animate nouns ‑sis is more common. Here the gun is grammatically inanimate (NI), so ‑ôs is the expected ending.

Trailforks pick: 'Six Shooter' (trail id 18858), Central Edmonton (South) / NW Edmonton — blue singletrack. Trailhead 53.52434, -113.54104. High confidence (Trailforks lists AKA ᓂᑯᒑᐧᓴᐢᑲᓅᐢ nikocwâsaskanôs explicitly).
